Main concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC granularity, audit log retention & redaction, KMS/HSM for key separation, and data residency/retention. topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-09
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Erin Black (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jenna Ortiz (Head of Security, Silvermark), Marcus Li (Platform Eng), Ravi Desai (CTO)

[00:00] Erin: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. i'm erin, i'm the AE on the account, and samir is our solutions engineer. quick check, audio ok?
[00:12] Jenna: yep, we can hear you. thanks for fitting us in, couple of us are in the office — so you might get background noise.
[00:18] Samir: no worries — i'll drive the technical bits. high level agenda, we want to understand your controls requirements and hosting preferences so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:27] Ravi: Sounds good. We're evaluating options for inference powering a few internal apps plus a customer-facing assistant. Main blockers for us are compliance evidence and key management.
[00:37] Marcus: Also we care about auditability — we need sufficiently detailed logs for forensic purposes and long retention for certain workflows.
[00:44] Erin: Perfect. maybe start with compliance baseline — Jenna, could you outline Silvermark's gating criteria?
[00:50] Jenna: Sure. we're SOC2 Type II in scope, pursuing ISO27001 cert next year. For procurement we need: (1) SOC2 report and audit manager contact, (2) a controls matrix showing which responsibilities remain with vendor vs us, (3) SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning, (4) ability to use our KMS for key separation ideally, and (5) audit log retention configurable to at least 2 years, with options to extend to 7 years for some records.
[01:18] Erin: That aligns with what we typically see. We can provide the SOC2 report and a controls matrix. For KMS — we support customer-managed keys in our Private offering, and for Dedicated we also have a KMS integration pattern. Hosted has envelope encryption with our keys by default but we can discuss bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options for enterprise.
[01:37] Marcus: Can you clarify BYOK on Dedicated vs Hosted? Does Hosted allow CMEK?
[01:42] Samir: Hosted standard doesn't give direct access to the raw HSM — we manage keys. But we do offer a customer-managed-keys path for enterprise customers which leverages cloud KMS with an external CMK or a wrapped key flow. For Dedicated, because it's reserved capacity for you, we support a more direct KMS integration and can arrange a key escrow pattern tied to your key policy. Private (VPC/on-prem) is the only model where you have full control over the key lifecycle and HSM.
[02:10] Jenna: Ok that helps. On audit logs — we need immutability guarantees and the ability to export logs to our SIEM. Do you push logs out or do we pull?
[02:20] Samir: We can do both. For Hosted and Dedicated we support streaming audit logs to your cloud logging (S3/CloudWatch/GCS) and syslog endpoints. We also keep an append-only internal audit trail. For Private, logs stay within your environment entirely. We can provide signed log chains if you need tamper-evidence.
[02:38] Ravi: Signed log chains — can you describe briefly?
[02:40] Samir: It's basically chained hashes over log segments with a signing key, so tamper attempts are detectable. We can export signed archives on request. Paste the spec in the follow-up doc.
[02:49] Jenna: Great. What about RBAC granularity? We need role separation — devs shouldn't see production keys or audit logs with PII.
[02:58] Erin: Our Console supports role-based access with scopes for model routes, datasets, and infra. SE, AE, and admin roles are examples. For enterprise we can align with SSO groups via SCIM to map into our RBAC. We also support token-scoped keys for ephemeral access.
[03:15] Marcus: Do tokens expire? We use short-lived tokens for CI/CD.
[03:18] Samir: Yes, you can configure TTLs and token rotation. For Private deployments you can tie tokens to your internal vault.
[03:24] Jenna: Any certifications or pen test evidence you can share?
[03:27] Erin: We'll share SOC2 Type II and our pen test summary PDF. ISO is in flight.
[03:31] Jenna: Good.
[03:33] Marcus: Data residency — we need to ensure inference data for EU customers remains in eu-west region and that any PII is either redacted before leaving our VPC or encrypted at rest with our keys. How would that work for Hosted?
[03:45] Samir: For Hosted we have regional endpoints; you can route requests to eu-west region and we can ensure model serving executes there. However by default logs and some telemetry may flow to centralized control plane; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated with region pinning or Private where control plane can be colocated. For PII we support request-side redaction and prefix/KV cache controls; you can mask fields client-side or use our built-in redaction passes.
[04:10] Jenna: When you say telemetry — do you mean usage metrics as well? We can't send raw prompt text off-shore for certain datasets.
[04:18] Samir: Right — we can disable or hash prompt-level telemetry. For enterprise we have a privacy config that strips or pseudonymizes prompts before they hit central logs. For absolute isolation, Private is the path.
[04:30] Ravi: Sounds like our risk appetite might prefer Dedicated initially, with Private for higher-sensitivity workloads. Can you summarize the tradeoffs in a doc?
[04:37] Erin: We'll include a tradeoff matrix in the follow-up: hosted = fastest onboarding, lower control; dedicated = more control, predictable throughput, KMS integration options; private = max control and residency but more ops.
[04:48] Jenna: Ok thanks. Another ask — key rotation policies. Our compliance requires rotation every 90 days for some keys. Can Redwood support forced rotation with zero-downtime?
[04:58] Samir: We have key rolling patterns. For Dedicated we orchestrate rotation via rewrapped keys and support a grace period for old keys for in-flight sessions. For Private you control rotation fully. We'll put the exact sequence diagram in the follow-up.
[05:12] Marcus: About logs again — retention windows. Our legal wants 7 years for certain transactional logs but we also want the ability to redact PII after 90 days. Is redaction reversible?
[05:24] Samir: Redaction is designed to be irreversible if you choose to irreversibly mask data. We also support pseudonymization where you can keep mapping tables in your KMS-protected store. So you can satisfy retention without keeping cleartext. We'll discuss options: irreversible hash vs reversible encryption under your key.
[05:44] Jenna: We will prefer irreversible redaction for user prompt text after policy window. Also need to confirm which fields you consider 'audit-relevant' — timestamps, model version, request metadata — do you include those by default?
[05:56] Samir: Yes, we log request metadata (timestamp, model id, version, route, tokens) by default. We can control including or excluding prompt text.
[06:05] Ravi: On SSO — our IDP is Okta, we need SAML SSO + SCIM. How mature is your SCIM implementation?
[06:12] Erin: SCIM provisioning is supported for group sync and user lifecycle. It's a standard SCIM 2.0 endpoint; we can map groups to RBAC roles out of the box. We'll include a sample SAML metadata file in the follow-up.
[06:24] Marcus: Are there audit logs for SCIM actions? We need a trail of who provisioned which role.
[06:29] Samir: Yes, provisioning actions are logged as admin events with actor identity and timestamp. Those go into the admin audit log stream.
[06:36] Jenna: Regarding encryption at rest — do you TLS between components and support customer-managed KMS keys for disk encryption?
[06:44] Samir: All in-transit is TLS. For disk-level encryption we rely on cloud provider disk encryption; for BYOK we integrate with KMS so payloads and artifacts can be encrypted under your keys. For Private, you can mount hardware HSMs.
[06:57] Ravi: Pen tests — you said you'd share the summary. Are there high severity items outstanding?
[07:03] Erin: Nothing critical currently. We'll send the executive summary and remediation timelines.
[07:08] Jenna: Great. One more thing — audit log immutability for legal eDiscovery. Do you support WORM or append-only retention in Hosted?
[07:18] Samir: For Hosted we can offer append-only logs with signed entries. For long-term WORM storage, we'd export to your cloud bucket with object lock enabled. For Dedicated and Private it's easier to guarantee by default.
[07:32] Marcus: What's the SLA around data deletion requests? If a user exercises right-to-be-forgotten, how quickly can logs be redacted?
[07:40] Samir: That depends on your retention policy. We can implement deletion workflows but note that for forensic logs we usually redact prompt-level PII and keep meta logs. We'll work with you on mapping retention windows to policy.
[07:53] Ravi: Ok. Pricing and procurement considerations — sensitive data customers usually opt for Dedicated. How long to pilot Dedicated? Is there a short eval?
[08:02] Erin: We often do a two-to-four week pilot on Dedicated with a modest reserved baseline. We can also run small-scale Private proof-of-concept in customer environment if needed. We'll include an estimate in the follow-up.
[08:14] Jenna: On the pilot, we need NDAs and data handling addendum before any live PII is used.
[08:20] Erin: Absolutely. We'll route the DPA/NDA through legal; i'll copy the relevant contacts.
[08:26] Marcus: A technical question — model drift and rollbacks. We require model versioning metadata in audit logs to trace responses to model versions.
[08:35] Samir: We include model id/version in logs and support automatic model pinning for routes. Rollbacks are an operational action and we record who initiated them.
[08:44] Jenna: Any limitations on token-level cost attribution? We need fine-grained billing by team and route.
[08:50] Erin: We provide token-level breakdowns and per-route billing in the console and via ingestable CSV exports. Billing data is separate from prompts.
[08:57] Marcus: Good. Another compliance ask — do you provide data processing agreements and subprocessors list? We have to review that for contract.
[09:04] Erin: Yes, subprocessors list and DPA are standard. We'll attach in our follow-up packet.
[09:09] Jenna: On identity, we also want MFA enforced for admin roles. Does Redwood enforce that?
[09:15] Samir: We support MFA enforcement for accounts. You can require it for RBAC roles and API key issuance flows.
[09:22] Ravi: Are there feature flags to disable model telemetry and usage logging for specific routes?
[09:27] Samir: Yes, route-level telemetry toggles are supported; you can disable telemetry or anonymize prompts for specific endpoints.
[09:33] Jenna: How about access to underlying KV cache? We worry about accidental leak of cached prefixes that include PII.
[09:40] Samir: KV cache is scoped per-tenant and per-route. You can opt-out of KV caching for sensitive routes. Also we support automatic cache scrubbing policies.
[09:50] Marcus: Ok would be good to get config examples for cache filtering and redaction rules.
[09:55] Samir: We'll put examples in the technical appendix.
[09:58] Jenna: Legal will want retention proof. Does Redwood have retention controls by log type?
[10:04] Erin: Yes, retention policies are configurable: admin events, request metadata, prompt store — each can have independent retention windows with export and purge hooks.
[10:12] Ravi: One last operational question — in Dedicated, who has access to the nodes? Can Redwood engineers SSH for debugging?
[10:20] Samir: For Dedicated, access is tightly controlled. We use jump hosts with audit logging and require customer approval for any live debugging sessions. For Private, we generally don't have access unless you explicitly grant it.
[10:34] Jenna: We need that documented for our procurement team.
[10:37] Erin: We'll include an ops access policy doc.
[10:40] Marcus: Good. Any customer references for similar compliance stacks?
[10:44] Erin: We can share anonymized references — especially in fintech and healthcare — i'll include a short list.
[10:50] Ravi: Awesome. Let's recap next steps. Jenna, you want SOC2 and controls matrix; Erin will provide; Samir will layout Dedicated config; Marcus will provide PII field list.
[10:58] Jenna: Correct.
[11:00] Erin: i'll follow up with an email by tomorrow and put the artifacts in a shared drive link. Samir and i will schedule the VPC deep-dive.
[11:08] Marcus: Thanks everyone.
[11:10] Jenna: Thanks.
[11:12] Erin: Thanks all.

Action items (recorded in transcript):
- Erin: send SOC2 report, pen test summary, DPA, subprocessors list, SAML metadata sample.
- Samir: Dedicated baseline config, KMS integration pattern, signed log chain spec, sample cache/redaction rules.
- Jenna: share PII fields list and retention windows.

End of meeting.
